Grid-connected to off-grid/islanding process: The PFMS monitors the voltage, frequency, and rate of change of frequency of the incoming power from the grid and compares that against the mini- mum and maximum allowable thresholds with the associated time durations. If the grid voltage, frequency, or rate of change of frequency are outside the allowable range for a sustained duration, the PFMS confirms the criteria for grid power being unstable as being met and disconnects the data center by opening breakers X and X . For this study, we implemented the thresholds and time u,1 u,2 durations as defined in IEEE 1547-2018. After disconnecting the data center power system from the utility, the PFMS then commands the available BESS units to initiate a black-start process in GFM mode to provide stable nominal voltage and frequency in the islanded power system. In this phase, the IT load is powered by the UPS while the cooling loads (not backed by the UPS) shut down. Once the BESS restores the nominal voltage and frequency on the medium-voltage power distribu- tion with a sufficient number of units online to support the data center load, the UPS units transfer the IT load to the BESS, and the cooling systems restart. Off-grid/islanded operation: In the case of a longer-duration outage from the grid, the data center power system will deplete the energy stored in the BESS units. As the median BESS SOC drops below a defined threshold SOC (SOC >SOC >SOC ), the PFMS would create alerts for the LS U LS L data center IT workload owner that the remaining energy on the BESS is limited, and the operator could consider shedding less critical compute workloads to increase the run time on the BESS. To simulate the action of the IT operator shedding lower-priority compute workloads, in this study, the multiplier of M=0.7 is used when the median SOC across the BESS units reaches below SOC .
